key_insight: SL-FAC reduces split-learning communication by compressing smashed data in the frequency domain and selectively transmitting the most informative frequency components, cutting bandwidth with little accuracy loss.
problem_solved: High communication overhead in split learning from transmitting large activations/gradients between many edge devices and the server, which limits deployment on bandwidth- and energy-constrained devices and reduces scalability.
method: Transform smashed data (activations/gradients) into a frequency domain representation and identify the most informative coefficients.
Apply frequency-aware compression (selective retention, quantization, sparsification) with adaptive bitrate per device to minimize transmitted payloads.
Server-side reconstruction and training-compatible compensation to preserve model accuracy while significantly lowering communication volume.
impact: Enables scalable, bandwidth- and energy-efficient split learning for edge deployments, allowing larger models and more devices to participate without major accuracy degradation or network cost increases.
visual_elements: Split-learning pipeline diagram showing device/server split, cut layer, and compressed smashed-data arrows with before/after size labels
Frequency-spectrum graphic indicating retained vs discarded frequency coefficients (e.g., heatmap or bar plot)
Trade-off chart comparing communication cost vs model accuracy for SL-FAC and baseline methods
Icon set: edge device, server, bandwidth meter, and a ‘split model’ symbol to convey infrastructure and savings
paper_title: SL-FAC: A Communication-Efficient Split Learning Framework with Frequency-Aware Compression
paper_authors: Zehang Lin, Miao Yang, Haihan Zhu, Zheng Lin, Jianhao Huang
